prompt.context: Smiles4Life is a regional dental company with 40 locations throughout Texas. The company is a dominant player in both Dallas and Houston, known to have especially strong ties to the Latin community. Last year, Smiles4Life did $60M in revenue with a 20% EBITDA margin after including corporate expenses. At this point, the owner/founder was ready to retire and decided to sell the company to Red Rock Capital, a PE fund based out of LA. Red Rock is excited about the new investment and is now focused on value creation. Red Rock engaged us to help diligence Smiles4Life and, being so pleased with their work, decided to engage us again to develop a growth strategy for its newest portfolio company.
prompt.question: How would you advise Red Rock Capital on a growth strategy for Smiles4Life?

clarifying_info.q: What is the growth target for this investment?
clarifying_info.a: Red Rock wants to increase EBITDA by 75% within three years of the investment.

clarifying_info.q: How does Smiles4Life generate revenue / what is the business model?
clarifying_info.a: Smiles4Life generates revenue much like any typical dental office. Doctors treat patients. Patients then pay either in cash or through a benefit provider (commercial PPO insurance, Medicaid, HMO, etc.).

clarifying_info.q: What is Red Rock Capital's background and experience?
clarifying_info.a: The PE fund focuses on investments across manufacturing, healthcare, and restaurants. It has successfully scaled many multi-site businesses before, especially in the restaurant industry.

exhibits.title: Estimated incremental results of multi-pronged digital program
exhibits.shows: A dual-axis chart showing LTM (last twelve months) website visits (bar chart, left axis) and LTM conversion rate (line chart, right axis) over time from 2014 to 2016, projecting the impact of a new digital marketing campaign.

exhibits.title: Average expected de novo performance and pipeline
exhibits.shows: A table showing projected annual office revenue and EBITDA contribution per new (de novo) store across Year 1 through Year 4, plus a proposed de novo opening schedule by year (2014-2017).

framework: Growth via existing customers / existing services (e.g., pricing, marketing, retention)
Growth via new customers / existing services (e.g., digital marketing, geographic expansion)
Growth via existing or new customers / new services (e.g., orthodontics, implants, whitening, in-house financing)
Geographic expansion: organic de novo store openings
Geographic expansion: acquisition of existing dental practices in new markets
Cost reduction levers: procurement, doctor/labor wages, centralization of customer service and claims management
Marketing funnel analysis (Awareness, Interest, Desire, Action) to drive top-line demand

questions.prompt: Digital marketing campaign: Management believes there is an opportunity to revamp marketing efforts, including a complete website overhaul and increased spend on SEO and targeted digital ads. Using Exhibit 1, what is the EBITDA opportunity from this initiative by year three? (Variable cost to see one incremental patient is 50% of revenue; average spend per dental appointment is $300.)
questions.guidance: Candidate should read LTM website visits (~450,000) and conversion rate (~4%) from the exhibit, multiply to get incremental appointments, then apply average spend and variable cost margin to calculate EBITDA. Strong candidates will contextualize the result against the $9M EBITDA target (current EBITDA $12M x 1.75 = $21M; incremental target = $9M).

math.setup: LTM incremental website visits by end of Year 3 x conversion rate = incremental appointments; appointments x avg spend = revenue; revenue x (1 - variable cost %) = EBITDA contribution
steps: LTM incremental website visits by end of Year 3 = 450,000
math.answer: $2.7M incremental EBITDA by Year 3, representing approximately 30% of the $9M EBITDA target

questions.prompt: What factors should the client consider as it develops and executes this new digital marketing initiative?
questions.guidance: Candidate should discuss customer segmentation (knowing who to target and what promotions they respond to), upfront and ongoing costs to update the website, and marketing ROI by channel (SEO, PPC, website, etc.).

questions.prompt: New stores (organic de novos): If the company pursues geographic expansion via organic growth, what is the EBITDA opportunity at the end of Year 3? Use Exhibit 2. Assume de novos open on January 1st of the respective year. Note: store EBITDA is higher than company-wide EBITDA margin because it does not include corporate expenses.
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate tenure of each cohort at end of Year 3, look up EBITDA per store from the exhibit, multiply by number of stores per cohort, and sum. It takes four years for a de novo to reach EBITDA maturity. Strong candidates will synthesize cumulative findings (marketing + de novos combined).

math.setup: For each opening year cohort, determine tenure at end of Year 3, read EBITDA/store from table, multiply by store count, sum across cohorts.
steps: 2014 cohort: 4 stores, tenure = 3 years, EBITDA/store = $350K → 4 x $350K = $1,400K
2015 cohort: 6 stores, tenure = 2 years, EBITDA/store = $300K → 6 x $300K = $1,800K
2016 cohort: 8 stores, tenure = 1 year, EBITDA/store = $200K → 8 x $200K = $1,600K
2017 cohort: not yet open by end of Year 3 → $0
Total EBITDA from de novos at end of Year 3 = $1,400K + $1,800K + $1,600K = $4,800K
math.answer: $4.8M incremental EBITDA by Year 3, representing approximately 53% of the $9M EBITDA target

questions.prompt: What are the opportunities and risks of the organic de novo expansion strategy?
questions.guidance: Opportunities: may be easier/less costly than acquisition; strong de novo playbook from 40 existing locations; potential to accelerate pipeline and pull 2017+ stores into the three-year horizon. Risks: market saturation (best locations may already be taken); operational burden of rapid expansion (hiring clinical staff, training, performance management).

questions.prompt: New market via acquisition: Management is interested in expanding into San Antonio. The business development team identified The Smile Center — 6 dental offices, each doing ~$1M in sales with a 20% EBITDA margin, representing ~$1.2M EBITDA. What are the opportunities and risks to consider? (No additional math required.)
questions.guidance: Opportunities: immediate access to cash flow and EBITDA ($1.2M = ~13% of target); economies of scale entering a new market (purchasing, regional management); likely revenue and cost synergies. Risks: deal costs hitting P&L; integration of people, processes, and culture; strategic fit (does target serve same customer segments?); comparative economics versus organic market entry.

math.setup: 6 stores x $1M revenue x 20% EBITDA margin
math.answer: $1.2M incremental EBITDA, representing approximately 13% of the $9M EBITDA target

brainstorming.prompt: What factors should the client consider as it develops and executes the digital marketing initiative?

categories.name: Customer Targeting
ideas: Customer segmentation — identify key demographics (Latin community, families, etc.) and tailor promotions accordingly
Understand which promotions or offers specific segments respond best to

categories.name: Cost & Investment
ideas: Ongoing investment in SEO and paid digital advertising
Cost of content creation and ongoing maintenance

categories.name: Channel Effectiveness
ideas: Marketing ROI by channel: SEO vs. PPC vs. website vs. social media
Attribution modeling to understand which channels drive appointments
A/B testing of landing pages and ad copy

categories.name: Execution & Operations
ideas: Internal capability vs. outsourced agency for digital marketing
Timeline and phasing of the rollout across 40 locations

recommendation: Begin execution on digital marketing campaign immediately, given the long ramp-up period to reach 450,000 LTM website visits and 4% conversion — this generates ~$2.7M EBITDA by Year 3 (30% of target).

Expand geographically via organic de novos per the proposed schedule; accelerating the 2017 pipeline into the three-year horizon would help ensure the $9M EBITDA target is met — de novos contribute ~$4.8M (53% of target). Combined with marketing, this reaches ~83% of the goal.

Further research the strategic and financial benefit of The Smile Center acquisition in San Antonio; while the standalone EBITDA is modest ($1.2M, ~13% of target), synergies could make this accretive and it provides immediate market presence in a new city.
risks: Market saturation in Texas could reduce the quality of available de novo locations
Integration risk and cultural fit with The Smile Center acquisition
Digital marketing ramp-up period means early years will see limited EBITDA contribution
Operational strain from simultaneous execution of multiple growth initiatives (hiring, training, management bandwidth)
next_steps: Finalize and launch digital marketing plan with clear channel ROI targets and conversion tracking
Stress-test the de novo site-selection process to confirm 'A' locations still exist; consider pulling 2017 stores into 2016
Conduct full strategic and financial due diligence on The Smile Center, including synergy analysis and integration planning
Define governance and KPIs to monitor progress against the 75% EBITDA growth target quarterly
